corpora.name: confirmation
notes: per-sequence wall time is recorded in metrics.sequenceWallMs (index = sequence seed)
hostile probes: 1 illegal event per step at p=0.35 + the full probe set every 11th step
deep freeze audit: every step shallow, depth-first on a 1-in-17 sample

corpora.name: tally
notes: ledger assembled directly (valid; the production ledger barrier re-verifies every record); control sample drives every event
tie-break pool includes the UTF-16/UTF-8 divergence pairs (U+1F600 vs U+FFFF, U+10FFFF vs U+FFFF)
ledger sizes: skewed 2..50 (median 5, mean ~12) with forced 2/3/49/50 boundaries

corpora.name: merkle
notes: sizes: log-uniform 1..2048 with forced boundaries 1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,1023,1024,1025,2047,2048
proof policy: ALL proofs for n <= 500, >= 10% evenly strided for n > 500
tamper matrix applied to every 10th verified proof (path flip/truncate/extend, wrong index, wrong leaf)

corpora.name: validator
notes: group signature cached per distinct message (4096 group signs, 4096-combo pool); every event has its own publisher signature and validation

matrix rows exercised: accept, accept-option-shape, attempt-content-divergence, batch-pin-mismatch, dispute-missing-tag, dispute-verdict-forgery, epoch-content-divergence, epoch-malformed, epoch-pin-mismatch, market-content-divergence, market-too-long, message-substitution, missing-epoch-tag, missing-signers-tag, nonce-mismatch, outcome-content-divergence, outcome-too-long, round-content-divergence, round-too-long, sig-truncated, sig-wrong-signer, signer-set-size-mismatch, signers-content-divergence, signers-malformed, signers-pin-mismatch, threshold-content-divergence, threshold-pin-mismatch, threshold-zero, tier-content-divergence, tier-out-of-range, tier-pin-mismatch, untrusted-publisher, wrong-group-key, wrong-kind
all keys are derived from the campaign seed (sha256 labels) — the run is reproducible, no CSPRNG

corpora.name: selection
notes: roster sizes: log-uniform 3..500, with 3/4/499/500 forced first in every run
deep checks (determinism, verifyJurySelection, independent ranking) on every 50th draw
chi-square: 100000 single-winner trials over an 8-juror weighted pool (df=7, p=0.001)

corpora.name: encoding
notes: field mixes of 1..8 fields over u8/u32/u64/text/hex/bytes with boundary and unicode values
injectivity + prefix-freeness checks on every 10th encoding
fail-closed boundary probes: 9 (both writers)

corpora.name: witness
notes: witness matrix rows: 27 (2 accept, 25 reject)
every unit drives a REAL case to round_resolved through the reducer (confirmations → challenge window → ladder round → resolve)
cases: rosters 3..7, quorum 1..N, maxLadderRounds 1..3, 1..3 accepted bonds, break-glass policy on for ~30% of units
rejected witnesses are asserted to leave BOTH the phase and the escalationLog unchanged (no reachable escalation)

corpora.name: epochRotation
notes: 25 batches per epoch → 40 cohorts, 39 rotations
real Schnorr cohort keys (sha256-derived per (seed, epoch)); every batch signature is a real FROST-manifest signature verified by the production verifier
rotations are chained through assertEpochRotationOrdering; same-key / skipped-epoch / backwards-window rotations are asserted typed refusals
cross-epoch re-batching is asserted LEGAL and independently verifiable (dedupe reputation by verdictHash, not by batch membership)

corpora.name: finality
notes: chain kinds: escalate-to-cap, concede-early, abort-window, expire-window (rotated by index)
every chain is driven end to end through the reducer: confirmations → challenge window → ladder rounds (escalations) → fee ledger → final
finality shapes: verdict recomputation, ledger provenance, real Schnorr batch manifest, case membership proof, epoch-pin and tamper refusals
terminal immutability: every terminal phase is asserted to refuse a PERFECT escalation witness and a tick

corpora.name: escalationTransport
notes: wire matrix rows: 91 (13 accept, 78 reject)
pool: 32 REAL driven cases — ladder round 1..4 × strict/legacy × break-glass/default × roster 3/5, every state reached through the reducer
digest injectivity is checked over EVERY accepted request in the run (digest → canonical preimage map)
the lone-surrogate rows prove the TextEncoder → U+FFFD byte collision is real, so the canonical-UTF-8 refusal is what keeps digests injective
T1: no raw throw escapes build/parse/serialize/map/reduce — every refusal is CourtConfirmationTransitionError

corpora.name: ledgerBarrier
notes: grid: 5984 cells (11 phases × 17 log shapes × 8 challenge shapes × strict/legacy × host/default)
stock: 643 reducer-reachable states across 11 phases, all captured by driving the real machine
the oracle is written from the invariant text in this file, not from the product code — a barrier and the oracle agreeing is a real cross-check
B1 protects users (a refused restorable snapshot bricks a live case); B2 protects value (an accepted forged ledger mints a verdict over records the machine never produced)
per-ledger scope: phase legality is the reducer guard (campaigns 1 and 9), and the mass-vote barrier applies only when the snapshot carries a ladder

corpora.name: bondAlgebra
notes: target rounds 1..5 (1, 2, 3, 4, 5 all exercised)
rosters are 7 seats; challengers are drawn 2..5 with DELIBERATE bond-pool collisions (repeated txids)
the ΔC schedule is checked against the geometric series 3^e, not against the package's own table
A1 one-hash-one-index, A2 no re-consumption, A3 strictly increasing rounds, A4 3^e growth, A5 consumption parity, A6 typed refusals only
